## Self-review / gap analysis (closing)

- **Containment, not sweep** — the check fails on *growth* (a file
  above its recorded count, or any site in an unnamed file) and
  advises on shrinkage; the 160-site recorded baseline is the
  sweep's starting debt, owned by P36.66a, and can only move down.
- **The rule is mechanical and honest about its edges** — quoted
  literals after comment-stripping, regex-literal quotes excluded
  by lookbehind, template literals counted by their leading literal
  run (`` `/r/${id}/` `` → `/r/$`). Sites the rule cannot classify
  (boundary-check `"/"` literals; the helper's own joins) are
  allow-listed with file+token+count+reason — capped, so a new use
  of the same token still counts; stale entries are named, never
  silently dropped.
- **The tripwire test is deliberate** — `BASE === "/"` fails the
  day a `base` is configured, forcing the snapshot row to re-assert
  the join shape; it is a config invariant, not a living-record pin
  (OM-15 holds).
- **Known limits recorded** — `srcset`-style multi-path attributes
  under-count per site but still count the file (containment holds
  at file granularity); a `//` inside a string followed by a later
  path on the same line is the documented under-count edge — the
  allow-list is the mechanism for anything the rule misclassifies,
  and a misclassification only ever *under*-counts (an allow-list
  entry with a reason corrects over-counting; an under-count means
  a site the sweep still owns). Zero client JS added; TypeScript
  confined to `web/` (SIG-ENG-010); `astro.config.mjs` read, not
  changed.
